nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis of NMO and Ir-NMO
nodes.procedure: The NMO and Ir-NMO were prepared via a facile hydrothermal approach, where the addition amount of Ir salt determines the molar ratio of Ir in Ir-NMO. The crystal structures were characterized by XRD, indexed to scheelite-type lattice of α-NiMoO4 (JCPDS No. 86-0361) with monoclinic space group C2/m.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectrum of Ir-NMO shows red-shift of Mo-O and Ni-O-Mo octahedral vibrations compared to NMO, indicating lattice expansion by Ir substitution.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Raman spectrum of Ir-NMO witnesses a red-shift associated with Mo-O and Ni-O-Mo octahedral vibrations in comparison with NMO, indicating the lattice expansion induced by Ir substitution at the octahedral sites.

nodes.characterization_summary: Both NMO and Ir-NMO show nanorod morphology (~50 nm diameter); Ir-NMO HAADF-STEM reveals atomically monodispersed bright Ir dots more intense than neighboring Ni atoms, confirming atomic incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Both NMO and Ir-NMO show typical nanorod morphology with diameters of ~50 nm ... the brightness of the Ir atom is more intense than that of the neighbouring Ni atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir-NMO (-221) plane interspace 0.3334 nm larger than NMO (0.3231 nm), confirming lattice expansion after Ir incorporation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) images show that the interspace of the (-221) plane of Ir-NMO (0.3334 nm) was larger than that of its counterpart without Ir (0.3231 nm), indicating that the lattice expansion occurs after incorporating Ir.

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental mapping by EDS shows homogeneous dispersion of Ir, Ni, Mo, O throughout Ir-NMO; 3D Gaussian fitting distinguishes atomic intensities.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Elemental mapping images show a homogeneous dispersion of Ir, Ni, Mo, and O atoms throughout the entire Ir-NMO sample ... the different atomic intensities can be clearly distinguished.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir 4f in Ir-NMO shows Ir3+ (62.0, 65.2 eV) and Ir4+ (62.4, 65.6 eV); Ni2+/Ni3+ ratio increases from 0.80 (NMO) to 1.16 (Ir-NMO); higher lattice oxygen ratio and positive O1 shift in Ir-NMO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Ir 4f spectrum of Ir-NMO could be deconvoluted into two sets of doublets at 62.0, 65.2 eV and 62.4, 65.6 eV ... Ir-NMO possesses a distinct higher ratio of lattice oxygen.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge XANES white line intensity of Ir-NMO between Ir foil and IrO2, close to IrO2 (+4 valence); Ni K-edge higher energy in Ir-NMO indicating higher Ni valency.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The white line intensity of Ir-NMO is located between the two references and close to IrO2 ... The Ni K-edge XANES of Ir-NMO reveals a higher photon energy compared with NMO.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ir L3-edge: Ir-O at 1.55 Å, Ir-Ni at 2.5 Å (shorter than Ir-Ir 2.7 Å); Ni K-edge: Ni-O 1.56 Å shorter in Ir-NMO than NMO; no Ir-Ir bonding confirms atomic dispersion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R-space Ir L3-edge extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra of Ir-NMO exhibit two characteristic peaks ... The absence of significant Ir-Ir bonding interactions strongly indicates the atomic-level dispersion.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman during OER shows Ni3+-O peaks at 474 cm-1 (Eg δNi-O bending) and 557 cm-1 (Alg νNi-O stretching) confirming γ-NiOOH formation; Ir-NMO initiates at lower potential (1.45 V vs RHE) than NMO (1.65 V).
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy was employed to monitor the dynamic changes of catalysts during OER operation ... Ir-NMO initiates Ni-O signals at 1.45 V (versus RHE), lower than that of NMO (1.65 V versus RHE).
